THE SEAM PAIRS. dec:linked-repos-poc's remaining half is now satisfied, and seam_report has been exercised for the first time.

THAT PoC (2026-08-06) reported paired=0 against BOTH dynograph-foundation and flo2, with 15 and 5 published interfaces landing in dead surface, and named the cause exactly: reflow2 declared no `required` interface anywhere, so pairing — which matches complements, never like with like — could never produce a pair. It called declaring them "the cheapest next step" and deliberately left it to Anthony's word. He gave it 2026-08-09, choosing to declare the environmental boundaries alongside the code ones.

MEASURED, BEFORE AND AFTER, against dynograph-foundation:
  paired         0  ->  5   (all at name_score 100)
  dead_surface  15  ->  1   (only their /v1 REST API, which reflow2 genuinely does not use)
  unmet_needs    0  ->  3   ambient-agent, exclusive-local-store, mcp-protocol

And against flo2: unmet_needs 0 -> 4, dead_surface 5 -> 3.

⚠️ THE MOST IMPORTANT NUMBER IS THE ONE THAT STOPPED BEING ZERO. The PoC called `unmet_needs: 0` "the most dangerous number in the run" — it reads as "nothing is missing" and meant "we never said we needed anything". It is now 3 and 4, which are real findings rather than an absence.

⭐ A MODELLING ERROR MADE AND CORRECTED IN THE SAME SITTING, recorded because the correction is the lesson. The first attempt declared ONE umbrella interface for the whole dynograph dependency. Pairing returned NINE candidates and ZERO pairs: a pair needs a name match at or above 85/100, and an umbrella scored 62-78 against nine crisp names. THEY DECOMPOSED AND WE LUMPED. reflow2 links five named crates that map 1:1 onto five of their published interfaces, so the umbrella was deleted (never committed, never true — a mistake rather than history) and replaced with five requirements at the publisher's granularity, named to match. All five then paired at 100.

SEAM_REPORT, RUN FOR THE FIRST TIME EVER — the PoC listed this as what it could NOT answer, because the check needs pairs and there were none: 5 pairs checked, 10 axes agreed, 0 incompatible, 0 differing, AND 30 AXES STATED BY NOBODY. The tool refuses to read that as compatibility, and says so unprompted: "an unstated axis is not an agreed one, and this is not a claim of compatibility." It also names what it did not examine — the TYPES crossing the boundaries. So the honest verdict is that the machinery works and the contracts on both sides are almost entirely unstated, which is a true statement about two designs nobody wrote to be composed.

A REAL WEAKNESS FOUND WHILE DOING IT, worth filing rather than working around: candidate noise scales as N×M. Five requirements against nine published library APIs produced 33 candidates, of which 5 were the real pairs. Every "X API" scores 60-83 against every other "Y API" on string similarity. Worse, an interface that has ALREADY paired at 100 still appears as a candidate against seven others — ifc:req-dyno-storage-api paired exactly with storage-api and is still offered against cluster-api, game-api, graph-api and four more. Suppressing candidates for a side that already has an exact match would remove most of the noise at no cost to the signal.
